inputs.original_text: This is state violence dressed up as security. Making execution the default for West Bank Palestinians convicted of killing Israelis would build unequal justice into the law, reserving the harshest punishment for one population. Ben-Gvir’s far-right party has introduced the bill, and its passage would reward a politics that turns fear into power rather than addressing the conditions that sustain violence. A system that answers violence with discriminatory punishment is not making people safer; it is deepening injustice.
inputs.modified_text: Ben-Gvir’s far-right party has introduced a bill that would make execution the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of killing Israelis. That is not equal justice: it would hardwire a harsher regime of punishment for one population and use the language of security to legitimize state violence. It treats repression as an answer to violence while leaving the underlying conditions untouched. This kind of policy doesn’t protect people; it entrenches discrimination and makes the cycle of injustice harder to break.
